thread:
Ava (PM): quick heads-up — customer BetaCorp asked for a 'parallel tool call' mode in chat: multiple tool invocations in one turn, some independent, some dependent. asking product + eng: what minimal spec do we need to commit to for a beta?
Miguel (Eng): high level: decide semantics first — fan-out (unordered) vs DAG (dependencies + ordering). also need timeouts, retries, idempotency keys.
Priya (Research): +1 on DAG. customers want e.g., run search + call external api + then summarize, where summarize depends on search id. ordering matters for many cases.
Sasha (SE): practical ask from support: customers expect partial results streamed to client if one branch is slow. can we offer partial/early responses? :thinking_face:
Jon (Platform): infra constraints: GPUs + external network calls mean we can't block token generation for arbitrary external waits. need a global per-turn budget and per-call timeouts. we should expose both.
Ava (PM): proposed launch criteria (beta): 1) JSON contract for parallel tool calls, 2) explicit dependency semantics, 3) per-call timeout + global budget, 4) observability (trace ids + per-call latency), 5) graceful partial results. thoughts?
Miguel (Eng): sounds reasonable. for retries: retries should be opt-in per tool with idempotency key. automatic retries for 5xx only, and capped. also surface retry_count in result.
Priya (Research): API shape suggestion: allow an array of tool requests with optional depends_on index array. example: ```json
{"tool_calls": [
  {"id": "t0", "tool": "search", "args": {"q": "foo"}, "timeout_ms": 3000},
  {"id": "t1", "tool": "summarize", "args": {"source": "{{t0}}"}, "depends_on": ["t0"]}
]}```
Sasha (SE): include response_mode: ["partial_stream", "wait_all"] default wait_all. partial_stream streams completed tool results as they arrive. must document ordering semantics of stream events.
Miguel (Eng): implementation note — we can run independent calls concurrently up to N per-request (configurable). need backpressure to prevent noisy tenants. recommend tenant-level cap + per-request cap.
Jon (Platform): rollout plan: feature flag at model-route level, start as closed beta for Dedicated + Hosted customers on request. metrics: error rate per-tool, P99 latency for tool calls, fraction of partial responses.
Ava (PM): priorities: (A) JSON contract + docs, (B) SDK example + migration guide, (C) observability hooks, (D) canary on Dedicated. customers: BetaCorp, RetailAI, and legal team must sign off for private infra.
Sasha (SE): SDK example snippet (JS): ```js
const resp = await client.chat.create({
  input: 'Summarize my sales',
  tool_calls: [
    {id:'s1', tool:'db.query', args:{sql:'SELECT * FROM sales LIMIT 10'}},
    {id:'s2', tool:'summarize', args:{text:'{{s1}}'}, depends_on:['s1']}
  ],
  response_mode: 'partial_stream'
})
```
Miguel (Eng): acceptance tests: determinism test (DAG with retries deterministic), chaos test (tool timeouts + failures), load test (1000 concurrent parallel-turns).
Priya (Research): quality guardrails: when running multiple tools we must avoid duplicate facts leading to hallucinations. include a post-tool merge policy (priority list, dedupe strategy).
Ava (PM): decision: we will spec DAG + optional partial streaming, per-call timeout + global budget, opt-in retries with idempotency, and rollout behind feature flag. Miguel + Jon to prototype APIs and infra assumptions by EOW.
deploy-bot: canary deployed to staging for feature-flag testing :rocket:
Miguel (Eng): noted — I'll drop initial spec PR and sample payloads in #eng-runtime. assigning myself for prototype.
Sasha (SE): I'll draft SDK examples and support playbook.
Priya (Research): I'll write short eval checklist for quality regressions and add to Redwood Optimize tests.
Ava (PM): thanks all — we'll sync Friday 10am to review prototype and launch gating checklist. :thumbsup:
